Solène Rowan
This gave rise to some controversial and arguably surprising outcomes. In one 
case, a building company constructed a house that turned out to be thirteen inches 
beneath the height required in the contractual specifications. The Aix-​en-​Provence 
Court of Appeal found that the breach did not relate to an essential term of the con­
tract and that the house was fit for purpose. It therefore declined the invitation to 
order that the house be demolished and rebuilt. This decision was quashed by the 
Cour de cassation: the injured party was entitled to compel the defaulting party to 
perform its obligations to the letter.58
In another case, the Aix-​en-​Provence Court of Appeal was found to have erred 
in refusing to order that a swimming pool built with three rather than the contrac­
tually specified four steps should be modified where the absence of the step did not 
impede access to the pool.59 Similarly, the Cour de cassation quashed a decision 
that a builder should not be compelled to make modifications to a house which, in 
breach of contract, had been constructed slightly out of alignment with the speci­
fied dimensions. It held that it was irrelevant that the difference between the work 
done and the work required was minimal.60
Whilst the new exception was introduced in response to these decisions, it has 
divided opinion amongst commentators. Some have welcomed the more moderate 
approach,61 arguing that to seek to enforce performance at all costs is an abuse of 
right (abus de droit).62 In contrast, those who favour the strict availability of spe­
cific enforcement have raised concerns that it is inconsistent with the binding force 
of contract and allows promises to be broken with impunity for no other reason 
than that the cost of performing is too high.63 Mekki, for instance, has said that the 
new exception is:
. . . too close to the solutions in common law systems. Enforced performance is a 
formidable weapon to encourage the promisor to perform. This exception sends 
a dangerous message to those promisors who might be tempted to breach their
